subject: Cost & burst agreement — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmecorp.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Recap from today — token volumes, budget band, burst needs & next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap so we're aligned and can get a formal proposal over to Finance: 

- Workload profile (as discussed): chat + routing + embeddings. Typical steady-state: ~200M tokens/month. Peak scenarios (product launches / marketing spikes): short bursts up to 550M tokens in a single day (we heard these are rare but critical).
- Access pattern: mostly request/response chat calls, median seq len ~750 tokens, embedding batch jobs overnight for enrichment.
- Current ask from Acme: target unit economics in the neighborhood of $/1M tokens (you mentioned Finance is aiming for ~$300/1M tokens for steady state).
- Quota & burst expectations: ability to burst 2.5x–3x baseline for up to 10 minutes during launches; need a soft-guarantee that bursts won’t be throttled without prior notice.

Next steps I'm proposing: 
1) We'll send a written proposal with two economics: a committed/discounted path (committed monthly or annual tokens) and a pay-as-you-go + burst policy for launches.
2) Presales (Jordan) will add concrete rate-limit numbers and overage tiers so Procurement can review legal and finance.
3) If the numbers look ok, propose a 30-minute follow-up call with Finance and Procurement by end of week.

I've attached the token estimate workbook we put together on the call; Jordan, Neha — please add the pricing sheet and proposed overage language (short bullets) in your follow-up.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmecorp.com>

Date: 2026-11-20T17:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap from today — token volumes, budget band, burst needs & next steps

Thanks, Ben — that matches what I took away. A few clarifications from Finance/Procurement: 

- Budget target: Finance would like to see a committed option at or under $300/1M tokens for our expected steady-state (200M/mo) with a path to deeper discounts if we commit to 12 months.
- Bursts: we understand burst pricing can be higher; Finance is comfortable with higher unit pricing during short bursts if there are clear caps and a predictable overage schedule.
- SLAs & throttling: critical for us is an explicit burst window (e.g., allowed bursts up to 3x baseline for ≤15 minutes without automated throttling) and an escalation path if throttling is applied.
- Lead time for quota increases: our infra team will want to know how quickly Redwood can raise a quota — typical scenarios could require a same-day or next-business-day increase for unexpected launch traffic.

Procurement uploaded a short checklist; I'm looping them for review. We'll need the written proposal + overage table to share with Finance by COB Monday.

Sarah
Sarah Li
Head of Product, Acme Corp
sarah.li@acmecorp.com | +1 (650) 222-3344
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap from today — token volumes, budget band, burst needs & next steps

Sarah — noted. Jordan and I discussed and we attached two artifacts: the Redwood pricing sheet (v2) and the token estimate workbook with your numbers filled in. High-level summary below so Procurement/Finance can triage quickly: 

- Committed tier (proposed): $275/1M tokens for a 12-month, 1B-token commit (equates to ~83M tokens/month). This tier scales with larger commits; we included a breakpoint table in the PDF.
- Pay-as-you-go (hosted): $420/1M tokens nominal.
- Burst/Overage: when customers exceed committed quota in a billing period, overage pricing will apply per token. For Acme's needs we propose a two-tier overage schedule: 
   • Short bursts (≤15 minutes, up to 3x baseline): 1.25x nominal unit price (for PAYG that would be $525/1M).
   • Sustained overages (beyond 15 minutes or >3x baseline): 1.75x nominal unit price.
- Quota increases: standard lead time is 3 business days for non-critical increases. For urgent launch-day increases we can support same-day scaling when notified 2–4 hours in advance and approved by our ops team (we treat these as exceptions and may require an emergency change order).

Jordan — can you drop a concise overage/legal-friendly paragraph we can include in the proposal? Neha — can you confirm the discounting matrix and whether we can get Procurement a demo of the console-level quota controls (rate limits page)?

Ben
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmecorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed overage & burst policy language + unit economics (attached)

Hi Sarah / team — attaching the two files Ben referenced. Below is the short-form language we recommend putting in the MSA/appendix for clarity. Procurement, feel free to adapt wording for legal: 

Proposed overage / burst appendix (short form):
- Baseline quota: A monthly committed quota (tokens) will be defined in Appendix A. Customer is billed on committed tokens at the contracted committed unit price.
- Burst allowance: Customer is permitted transient bursts up to 3x the committed per-minute request rate for up to 15 continuous minutes without applying sustained overage pricing. Bursts beyond this window or sustained overuse will be billed at the overage rate in Appendix B.
- Overage rates: Overage charges will be calculated on a per-token basis. Short-burst overage = 1.25x the current PAYG unit price. Sustained overage = 1.75x the current PAYG unit price.
- Throttling & escalation: Redwood will not automatically throttle within burst allowance. In the event of platform-wide constraints, Redwood will (a) fallback to agreed alternate model variants where possible and (b) notify Customer with an incident ticket and a live ops contact. Emergency quota increases can be requested via the Redwood Console or by contacting Redwood Ops; typical SLA for emergency requests is 4 hours.
- Billing reconciliation: Any overage charges will be itemized on the monthly invoice and available in the Console. Disputed charges may be investigated within 30 days.

Unit economics summary (illustrative):
- Committed (12m / 1B tokens): $275 / 1M tokens
- Committed (12m / 2B tokens): $240 / 1M tokens
- PAYG (no commit): $420 / 1M tokens
- Short-burst overage: 1.25x PAYG (=> $525 / 1M tokens)
- Sustained overage: 1.75x PAYG (=> $735 / 1M tokens)

Notes: these are initial figures — Neha, I'm flexible on the committed breakpoint and can tighten the committed price for a larger multi-year commit. Also attaching a short GIF of the Console's quota controls so you can see how to submit an emergency increase request.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Thanks — received and shared internally. A few quick notes from Finance: committed at $275/1M is promising if we can hit the 1B annual minimum (they asked for a projection of how we get there). Procurement will review the appendix and follow up with redlines; they'll likely ask for a 30–60 day billing dispute window and a clearer escalation SLA for emergency quota increases.

We'll aim to get a consolidated response by COB Tuesday (Nov 24). If we need a quick sync earlier, I'll ping for a 15-min slot.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

— Sarah
